Welcome to Ashley Park School
Ashley Park and Skylarks have come together to create a clear, supportive education pathway.
Welcome to Ashley Park School
Ashley Park School is set across two sites, both offering high-quality, specialist SEND education from primary years right through to sixth form.
Everything we do is tailored to offering each young person the best possible educational experience. All pupils will be supported to learn at their own level through personalised teaching and differentiated lessons based on the National Curriculum.
Ashley Park (Primary Site)
Our primary site provides a nurturing and purposeful learning environment for pupils aged 5 to 11 with a diagnosis of autism. We aim to deliver a child-centred education that recognises individual potential, fosters independence, and ensures each pupil is supported to achieve their best.
Ashley Park/Skylarks (Secondary Site)
Our secondary site provides a supportive and inspiring learning environment for young people aged 11 to 18 with a diagnosis of Autism. We are committed to delivering personalised pathways that equip each student with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to thrive both in school and beyond.
© Outcomes First Group 2026

Home Our Approach Primary Curriculum
Curriculum
At Ashley Park School, every child’s learning journey is unique. Our curriculum is designed to nurture individual strengths, remove barriers to learning, and prepare pupils for happy, independent futures.
We combine three strands – EHCP provision, therapy, and academic learning – to create a truly personalised approach. With small class sizes and highly skilled staff, we provide the right balance of support and challenge to help every pupil thrive.
Pupils follow one of three flexible pathways – Discovery, Explorer or Adventure – depending on their individual needs and aspirations. These are reviewed regularly to make sure each child continues on the best route for their development.
Our Skylarks site provides a dedicated secondary-specific environment where pupils can continue their learning journey, access specialist teaching, and work towards accredited qualifications and exams in a setting that promotes confidence, independence, and aspiration.
Together with families, we create a curriculum that equips every young person with the skills and confidence to succeed in life.
© Outcomes First Group 2026

Home News & Events Ashley Park and Skylarks School Are Merging to Create a Unified Education Pathway
Ashley Park and Skylarks School Are Merging to Create a Unified Education Pathway
We’re delighted to share some exciting news: Ashley Park School in Walton-on-Thames and Skylarks School in Epsom are merging to create a single, joined-up education pathway for children and young people aged 7 to 19 years old.
This strategic development brings together the strengths of both schools, ensuring that families in Surrey and the surrounding areas have access to high-quality, specialist SEND education from primary years right through to sixth form.

Home About Us Our Team
Meet our Team
Welcome to Ashley Park School
We’re excited to share that Ashley Park and Skylarks School have joined together to create one unified education pathway for children and young people aged 6-19. This means we can offer even greater continuity, stability, and opportunities for every pupil as they move through their learning journey.
Ashley Park will continue to be our nurturing hub for primary-aged pupils, while Skylarks will focus on secondary and post-16 education. Together, we’ll provide a smooth transition between each stage, helping every child feel confident, supported, and ready for what comes next.
With one dedicated leadership team and a consistent approach to learning, therapy, and care, our goal is to ensure every pupil receives the right support, in the right place, at the right time – while also making life easier for families.
We’re really looking forward to this next chapter and to keeping you updated as we grow and develop together.
Thank you for being part of our community.
Barry New – Headteacher, Skylarks Site
Ruth Bodley – Head of School, Ashley Park
© Outcomes First Group 2026

Complaints
We take all complaints seriously. We have a full complaints policy and procedure, which is available from the school office or for download above. Initial complaints should be made to the Headteacher, Barry New, via telephone on 01932 379043 or via email to info@ashleyparkschool.co.uk or admin@skylarksschool.co.uk.
If the complaint is concerning the Headteacher, please contact Lorna Davies-Bailey, Regional Director, via email at lorna.davies-bailey@ofgl.co.uk.

Home About Us Proprietor
Proprietor
Ashley Park School is operated by P Bloom Ltd
Ashley Park School is owned by Options Autism 7 Ltd and is a fully owned subsidiary of P Bloom Ltd, which is part of Outcomes First Group, a provider of children’s services in the UK.
Ashley Park School has its own dedicated management team under the leadership of Barry New. Oversight of school management is provided by the Assistant Regional Director for Options Autism, responsible to the Operations Director, Richard Adams-Murgatroyd, and Chief Executive Officer, Richard Power.
Richard Power also acts as the registered Proprietor Chairperson for P. Bloom Ltd.
The management team is complemented by Group support functions covering Quality and Compliance, Admissions and Marketing, Human Resources, Finance and IT. Key decisions are referred to Outcomes First Group’s Board of Directors, consisting of Outcomes First Group CEO, David Leatherbarrow and CFO, Jean-Luc Janet, together with an independent Chairman and three Non-Executive Directors.

What we do
At both Ashley Park and Skylarks, our mission is simple: to help every young person flourish.
We want our pupils to grow in confidence, achieve strong educational outcomes, and develop the skills and aspirations that will raise hopes for the future.
Personalised Education
We provide specialist education and therapeutic support tailored to a wide range of needs. Lessons are carefully designed around the National Curriculum, adapted so that every pupil can learn at their own pace and level. Alongside academic study, pupils can work towards accredited qualifications, vocational pathways, and life skills courses, ensuring they are well prepared for life beyond school.
